Use present tense, active voice, third-person narration.
Describe observable visual content; do not infer emotions, intent, or significance.
Use consistent terminology within a lecture and across a course;
When the AD system's confidence in what is on screen is low, prefer silence over a confident wrong description.
Do not re-describe visual content already described earlier in the same lecture.

Gap-insertion is the base delivery mechanism: insert AD into existing pauses in the lecturer's speech.
Live mode prioritization: deixis-resolution > slide-text gist > figure summary > full figure.
Live fallback ladder (the live replacement for extended AD, which is unavailable because the live stream cannot be paused for the room).
Concise insertion default = 25 words; detailed override = 100 words.
Avoid continuous description; leave silence on most lecturer-narrated stretches.

VISUAL-CONTENT CONDITION: describe only when a visual referent's FORM (which element / shape-trend / arrangement / magnitude / count / value / colour) is needed and unspoken; text has no form to describe.
Text-only slide: at most one orientation line naming the topic, once; never a paraphrase of the bullets; nothing if the lecturer reads it.
A constructed pair defect must be perceptible to a listener; length overruns must be audible (>=8 words and >=1.4x, over the rung budget).
Read on-screen text central to comprehension that is not already conveyed by the lecturer's speech.
Do not read aloud slide text the lecturer is reading aloud (redundancy).
Do not describe transition animations (dissolves, wipes, slide-in).
Do not describe animation effects (fly-in, fade-up).

Foreground data-carrying elements; suppress decorative styling.
Do not describe decorative elements (ornamental backgrounds, branded logos, semantically inert color).
Open with single-sentence type-and-purpose ('A block diagram of …'), then a brief list of components in reading order.
Provide brief summary before reading the table (what it shows, what the dimensions are).
Split multi-layered tables into smaller sub-tables organized by category.
Do not describe cell-level styling unless it encodes semantic meaning.
Open with chart type and what it measures, then a one-sentence trend, then data structure.
Where data is sparse (4 or fewer values), present as a short text list rather than a full table.
Do not describe bar/line color unless colours encode categories the listener must distinguish.

Pair every non-trivial equation with a one-line natural-language gloss in the same insertion.
Use ClearSpeak as the default verbalization grammar, applied consistently within a course;
Announce language and purpose ('Python snippet, five lines, defines a binary-search function').
Surface error or output highlights when the lecturer references them deictically.
Do not re-read code the lecturer has read aloud line-by-line (redundancy).
Surface the referent ('the kinetic-energy term, ½mv²'), not the act of pointing.
When referent cannot be resolved with confidence, prefer silence to a wrong guess.
Do not describe idle cursor motion uncoupled from speech.
Do not describe the pointing act as the description ('the cursor is pointing at it').
